required_fixes: Fix C2 specification mismatch if re-preregistering: frozen decision_rule requires strict monotonicity F(20)>F(15)>F(10)>F(5) (spec.json:decision_rule C2_STEP_FUNCTION_STRUCTURE) but prereg text and hypothesis describe 'monotonic increase from n=10 to n=20' (prereg.md:Analysis Protocol Step 3, report.md:Interpretation). Under frozen rule C2 FAILS because F(10)=F(5)=0.0; under the intended n10->n20 rule C2 would PASS (0.0<0.4996<0.5654). Any future design must choose one definition and keep it consistent across hypothesis, falsifier, and decision_rule.

Do not use linear extrapolation for the bounded proportion F(n)=proportion(margin>0) in [0,1]. The frozen method slope from n=15->n=20 (0.01316/element) predicts F(50)=0.9602 and F(82)=1.3813 (>1.0 physically impossible per result.json:metrics.c3_extrapolation). All alternative linear anchors also exceed 1.0 (n5->n20 gives 1.696, n10->n20 gives 2.262 per result.json:metrics.alternative_extrapolations). Future non-parametric extrapolation must use a bounded form (e.g., logistic, Hill, Richards) or explicitly model saturation rather than piecewise linear.

Treat the empirical CDF mapping as the diagnostic identity under template invariance, not as an independent extrapolable model. Producer result.json:metrics.baseline_comparison and report.md correctly note F(n) IS proportion(margin>0) which equals ranking agreement exactly by construction (positive_control residual 0.00pp at all n). It provides zero predictive information beyond the parent diagnostic and cannot be validated beyond training points without full-DOM data. Do not cite C1 PASS (trivial by construction) as model validation.

For any future full-DOM claim, prioritize Docker-based direct measurement (EXP-INTEL-35462974425, image am1n3e/webarena-verified-shopping:latest) over modeling from n=5-20. Four consecutive model-based approaches have now failed C1/C2: Phi(mean(SNR_i)) 40-50pp, Phi(mean/std) 17.8pp, Phi(median/std) 34.59pp/18.96pp, sign-fraction power law 12.39pp/R2=0.8797, and now empirical CDF linear extrapolation physically impossible. This is model-misspecification due to step-function (0,0,0.50,0.57) / 7.6x deceleration, not a tunable parameter issue.

The discrepancy is a specification design flaw, not an infrastructure or computation error. Verdict MEASUREMENT_INVALID via C1 AND NOT C2 is the correct frozen outcome.

claim_ceiling: MAX JUSTIFIED: The empirical CDF mapping F(n)=proportion(margin_i>0) reproduces observed ranking agreement exactly at n=5 (0.0), n=10 (0.0), n=15 (0.4996), n=20 (0.5654) within 0.00pp (C1 PASS) but this is trivially true by construction under template invariance where ranking agreement equals proportion(margin>0) exactly; it is the diagnostic identity, not a validated predictive model, and adds zero information beyond the parent positive control. The step-function structure (0,0,0.50,0.57) exhibits a sharp jump n10->n15 (0.4996, 88.4% of total increase) and plateau n15->n20 (0.0658, 11.6%) with 7.6x growth deceleration (ratio 0.1317), consistent descriptively with a threshold/phase-transition but unvalidated as a predictive rate. Under the frozen strict-monotonicity rule C2 FAILS because F(10)=F(5)=0.0 (C2 requires F20>F15>F10>F5); descriptively F is strictly increasing from n=10 to n=20 (0.0<0.4996<0.5654). Linear extrapolation from n15->n20 slope (0.01316/element) is INVALID: it predicts F(50)=0.9602 and F(82)=1.3813 (>1.0 impossible), and all alternative linear anchors also exceed 1.0, demonstrating bounded-quantity misspecification. Therefore C3 FAILS and no validated extrapolation to full DOM n=50/82 is justified; the hypothesis that an empirical CDF / non-parametric mapping provides a validated extrapolation path within 10pp is NOT supported. Full-DOM ranking stability at n=21-82 remains UNKNOWN. The only product-grade fact established is the descriptive plateau at truncated-first-20 on this single Magento site with tag_entropy x DEF-FULL-MAP: canonical agreement 0.5654 at n=20 (56.5%) with diminishing returns from n15. No inference that the plateau persists below 80% at full DOM is justified from linear extrapolation; the 7.6x deceleration is hypothesis-generating only. Docker-based direct full-DOM measurement (EXP-INTEL-35462974425) remains the only path to an empirical answer; the failure of four consecutive model-based approaches (Phi(mean(SNR_i)), Phi(mean/std), Phi(median/std), sign-fraction power law, now non-parametric linear) strengthens the case to bypass modeling.

Whether the frozen C2 specification flaw (strict monotonicity across n=5->n=10 where F=0 tie vs intended monotonicity from n=10->n=20) should be corrected in a future preregistration remains open; under corrected rule C2 would PASS and the frozen verdict would be C1 AND C2 AND NOT C3 -> EMPIRICAL_CDF_PREDICTS_CROSSING, but that crossing prediction would still be invalid due to bounded-quantity misspecification.

Whether the 7.6x growth deceleration (plateau/jump=0.132) and marginal sign crossing from -1.35e-04 at n10 to +2.66e-05 at n15 reflect a genuine threshold/phase-transition or an artifact of the narrow n=5-20 range with only 4 points is UNKNOWN; fitting a bounded saturating function (logistic, Hill, Richards) to these 4 points could be tested but is outside frozen spec and would have only 2 df.
Whether template invariance breaks at full DOM element counts, changing the variance structure and invalidating proportion(margin>0) as the data-generating process, remains UNTESTED.
Cross-site generalization beyond single Magento Docker site remains UNTESTED.
Whether per-task recipe (78.65% at n=20 per EXP-INTEL-35445596324) achieves >=80% at full DOM remains UNKNOWN and outside this experiment's truncated-first-20 scope.
The minor provenance discrepancy for n_zero counts at n15 (producer 0 vs raw 1230) and n20 (producer 0 vs raw 599) does not affect verdict but should be reconciled for artifact hygiene.
